# Beginner · the idea

## What changes, what stays {#changes-stays}

{{< include /_macros.qmd >}}

::: {.columns}
::: {.column}
**What changes**

- new spectrum: 7–24 GHz ("upper mid-band")
- downlink and uplink at the same time on one TDD carrier
- AI helping to predict beams and channels
- the network sensing its surroundings like a radar
- satellites as part of the network
:::
::: {.column}
**What stays**

- link budgets and propagation
- cyclic prefix, Doppler and phase noise
- synchronization
- antenna and beam physics
- amplifier linearity
:::
:::

::: {.box}
[The one idea of this section]{.box-title}
Master the fundamentals of this course and every new release becomes an extension, not a restart.
:::

# Intermediate · how it works

## What 5G-Advanced changes for RF engineers {#outlook}

::: {.compact}
| Topic | Release | RF impact |
|---|---|---|
| Network energy saving | Rel-18 | cell/antenna muting, PA efficiency at low load |
| Sub-band full duplex (SBFD) | Rel-18 study, Rel-19 | DL and UL in one TDD carrier: self- and cross-link interference |
| AI/ML for beam management and CSI | Rel-18 study, Rel-19 | beam prediction from partial measurements (set A/B) |
| NTN (satellite) | Rel-17 onward | Doppler, long delay, new link budgets |
| Upper mid-band (7–24 GHz) | 6G studies, Rel-20 | new arrays, propagation, coexistence |
:::

::: {.small}

The fundamentals of this course (CP and Doppler, sync, link budget, beam gain, linearity) carry over unchanged.

:::

::: {.notes}
ShareTechnote has pages on AI/ML beam management that describe the Set A (observed) and Set B (predicted) framework from the Rel-18 study and Rel-19 RRC parameters. Release timing changes; check 3GPP's release planning page for the current freeze dates.
:::

# Advanced · expert depth

## Course map: one number per section {#course-map}

::: {.compact}
| Chapter | Numbers to remember |
|---|---|
| 1 · Air interface | T~c~ = 0.509 ns; CP 4.69 µs × 2^−μ^; 845 kHz guard at 100 MHz/30 kHz; 2 GP symbols ≈ 10.7 km; ≤ 3 µs sync |
| 2 · Finding the network | 240 × 4 SSB REs; PCI = 3N~ID~^(1)^ + N~ID~^(2)^; R ≈ c·min(CP, GT)/2; 6.67 µs per km |
| 3 · Measuring the radio | RSRP = per RE; RSRQ ≤ −10.8 dB at full load; UL ends where RSRP still looks good; ≈ 39 dB/decade urban NLOS |
| 4 · Beams and hardware | EIRP = P~PA~ + 20·lg N + G~e~; HPBW ≈ 101.5°/N; +20·lg N phase noise; PAPR ≈ 12 dB; EVM adds in RSS |
:::

# Practice

## Reflection questions {#ex}

1. Sub-band full duplex puts downlink and uplink on one TDD carrier at the same time. Which topics from Chapter 1 (sync, cross-link interference) become harder, and why?
2. At 7–24 GHz, which effects from this course grow and which shrink compared with 3.5 GHz?
3. Pick one cell you know. Which single section of this course would most improve its performance if applied?

::: {.aside-note}
Open questions: discuss them in the comments of the series, or with your team.
:::

::: {.notes}
1. SBFD makes cross-link interference intra-cell and inter-cell at once: the gNB's own transmitter leaks into its receiver (self-interference, needing tens of dB of isolation and cancellation), and neighbours' DL lands on UL sub-bands at all times, not only at pattern mismatches.
2. Grows: free-space loss, O2I penetration, phase noise, Doppler per km/h. Shrinks: antenna size per gain (more elements per panel), CP needs (smaller cells, narrower beams).
3. Open answer.
:::
